title: Mission 2 Assessment: Time and Verb Forms (Class 10)
subtitle: Answer all 10 questions on Past Time sequences, Present Perfect duration, Sequence of Tenses, and Future Time expressions.

questions.questionText: When we reached the railway platform, the Konark Express _____ already _____.
questions.explanation: Between two past actions, the earlier action (the train leaving) takes Past Perfect ('had left'), while the later arrival takes Past Simple ('reached').
questions.learningObjective: Past Simple vs Past Perfect (earlier past)

questions.questionText: Choose the accurate sentence expressing an unbroken duration from the past up to today:

options.text: Dr. Sen is teaching chemistry here since 2016.
Dr. Sen has been teaching chemistry here since 2016.
Dr. Sen taught chemistry here since 2016.
Dr. Sen teaches chemistry here since 2016.

questions.explanation: 'since 2016' marks a starting point continuing into the present, requiring Present Perfect or Present Perfect Progressive ('has been teaching').
questions.learningObjective: Connecting past start to present time

questions.questionText: Which option completes this reported universal truth accurately? 'In yesterday's assembly, our principal reminded us that light _____ faster than sound.'
questions.explanation: Under the Sequence of Tenses, universal truths and scientific laws stay in Present Simple ('travels') even when the reporting verb ('reminded') is in the past.

questions.questionText: By 4:30 p.m. tomorrow, the student volunteers _____ all the saplings along the canal.
questions.explanation: 'By 4:30 p.m. tomorrow' sets a future deadline before which the action completes, expressed by 'will have + V3' ('will have planted').

questions.questionText: Pointing to dark monsoon clouds overhead, Arjun says, 'Take your umbrella—it _____ very soon.' Which future form matches visible present evidence?
questions.explanation: Odisha Class X highlights 'be going to + base verb' when present physical signs (dark clouds) show what is about to happen.

questions.questionText: Read the sentence: 'While Mira was sketching the banyan tree, a sudden breeze _____ her notebook.' Choose the accurate verb.
questions.explanation: When an ongoing past background action ('was sketching') is interrupted by a short event, the interrupting action uses Past Simple ('blew').

questions.questionText: Identify the sentence that uses a stative verb correctly without breaking tense rules.

options.text: Our school library has owned these rare manuscripts since 1998.
Our school library is owning these rare manuscripts since 1998.
Everyone in Class 10 is knowing the solar system diagram.
These fresh mangoes are costing less in summer.

questions.explanation: State verbs ('own', 'know', 'cost') avoid '-ing' progressive forms. 'has owned ... since 1998' accurately uses Present Perfect for duration up to now.

questions.questionText: Which pair of clues correctly distinguishes 'for' from 'since'?
questions.explanation: 'for' is used with a measured duration ('for three years'), while 'since' is used with a specific starting point ('since 2020').

questions.questionText: Spot the error in this Class 10 archive draft: 'Before the chief guest arrived, the choir had already sang the welcome song.'

options.text: After 'had', the past participle 'sung' (V3) must be used instead of Past Simple 'sang' (V2).

questions.explanation: Past Perfect requires 'had + V3': sing (V1) → sang (V2) → sung (V3), so 'had already sung' is correct.
questions.learningObjective: Diagnosing irregular V3 and tense errors

questions.questionText: Compare these two notices: (1) 'The bus leaves at 7:00 a.m. tomorrow.' (2) 'I am meeting the science coach at 4:00 p.m. tomorrow.' Why are BOTH accurate?

options.text: Present Simple expresses a fixed public timetable, while Present Progressive expresses a personal arrangement in future time.
Both sentences actually refer to yesterday morning.
English has no verb forms for public timetables.
'tomorrow' forces every sentence to become Past Simple.

questions.explanation: Odisha Class X Ch. 1 explicitly shows how Present Simple expresses official schedules/timetables and Present Progressive expresses arranged personal future plans.
